correctness.rationale: Each edge has 2(d-1) neighbours, so a strong-majority 2-colouring is exactly an edge-signing with zero sum on each edge neighbourhood. The incidence identity T(x)+T(x+e_i)=2s_i(x) gives (d-2)T+AT=0. Walsh characters diagonalize cube adjacency with eigenvalues d-2|S|, forcing T into the d-dimensional level-(d-1) space. Averaging T across an i-edge retains exactly coefficient a_i, whence s_i=a_i chi_[d]\{i} and each a_i must be a sign; every sign tuple conversely balances all neighbours. The translation action on tuple exponents has matrix I+J over F2; its rank is d for even d and d-1 for odd d, establishing the orbit count. Brute-force all \(2^4\) and \(2^{12}\) assignments on Q2 and Q3 gives 4 and 8 valid signings; all formula families were independently checked through d=8. Finite checks are not used in place of the proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact classification for the natural, unbounded-dimensional family of binary hypercubes, rather than a small numerical special case: it determines the optimum two-colour index, the entire set of colourings, exact counts and parity-dependent automorphism orbits. The Fourier reduction proves strong structural rigidity despite an exponentially increasing edge set, and the odd/even orbit dichotomy identifies a discrete global obstruction not available from generic upper bounds. The same signed-incidence mechanism is potentially reusable for other symmetric graphs, although no such extension is claimed.
